title: Fetch request configuration
learningObjectives: Explain fetch request configuration and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: fetch accepts a URL and options such as method, headers, body, credentials, cache, mode, redirect, and signal. JSON request bodies are commonly created with JSON.stringify and an application/json Content-Type header.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit configuration makes requests predictable. Sensitive operations still require backend authorization and suitable CSRF protections.
understand.analogy: Request options are instructions attached to the request: method, headers, content, and delivery rules.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The example sends JSON to an illustrative same-origin endpoint; production code must inspect status and handle the response.

examples.explanation: The example sends JSON to an illustrative same-origin endpoint; production code must inspect status and handle the response.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Build GET and POST examples. Explain when a request body is appropriate and why credentials must not be exposed casually.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.

questions.prompt: How is an object commonly sent as a JSON request body?
questions.explanation: JSON.stringify serializes the object and Content-Type describes the body format.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach to network-driven UI?
options: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
Assume every fulfilled fetch means HTTP success
questions.answer: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
questions.explanation: Explicit states and bounded recovery make network interfaces predictable and safe.
